newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: DB ceo not confident of matching H1 in H2.
newsitem.headline: DB ceo not confident of matching H1 in H2.

text.p: DB Group chief executive Erik Korthals Altes said he was not overly confident the company would match an eight percent-plus increase in profitability experienced in the first half over the second half.

Asked if he expected a better second half, Korthals Altes said, "That would be nice, but we know what we did in the first half and I'm not overly confident that we will be able to maintain that eight-plus (growth) in the rest of the year," he said.
"From operations, it is not going to be easier," he told a news conference.
Last winter was "terrible" in terms of volumes but DB expected to pick up a little this winter.
"But still, DB line volumes in April were 10 percent down on the previous year. May was six percent down on the previous year," the chief executive said.
"So we believe that towards the next four months we will have a bit of a levelling but for the whole year we will probably look to be 4.5-to-5.0 percent in decline (in consumption)," he said.
"It's tough out there and there is always a danger that people are trying to resolve things through price cutting, and that is eating into your margins and not bringing in any extra volume," he said.
